task_spec.title: Simulation Task
task_spec.description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

RMSE.description: Root Mean Square Error measuring overall predictive accuracy of mask adoption rates
RMSE.interpretation: Directly interpretable as percentage deviations due to the 0-1 range

interactions.name: peer_influence
interactions.description: Persons observe the mask status of their neighbors; if perceived support exceeds their threshold (or via a logistic decision rule), they adopt.

interactions.name: social_reinforcement
interactions.description: Repeated exposures from multiple neighbors increase the probability of adoption (complex contagion).

interactions.name: information_broadcast
interactions.description: Public health authority and media broadcast messages that shift risk perception and adoption propensity.

interactions.name: policy_mandate_enforcement
interactions.description: Mandates increase perceived benefits or costs of non-compliance; enforcement and penalties affect adoption and dropout.

interactions.name: tie_rewiring_homophily
interactions.description: People rewire social ties based on homophily in mask status or beliefs, affecting diffusion pathways.

interactions.name: location_based_contact
interactions.description: Contacts are modulated by shared locations (households, workplaces, etc.), altering exposure frequency.

metrics.name: adoption_rate_over_time
metrics.description: Proportion of agents wearing masks at each time step.

metrics.name: final_adoption_rate
metrics.description: Proportion of agents wearing masks at the end of the simulation.

metrics.name: time_to_50_percent_adoption
metrics.description: Number of steps until at least 50% of agents adopt mask-wearing.

metrics.name: cascade_size
metrics.description: Total number (or share) of adopters ultimately influenced by initial seeds.

metrics.name: behavior_reproduction_number_Rb
metrics.description: Average number of new adopters directly attributable to a single adopter within a short window.

metrics.name: adoption_churn_rate
metrics.description: Rate at which adopters drop the behavior per time step.

metrics.name: mean_exposures_before_adoption
metrics.description: Average number of neighbor exposures required before an agent adopts.

metrics.name: assortativity_by_adoption
metrics.description: Network assortativity coefficient based on mask adoption status.

metrics.name: inequality_of_adoption
metrics.description: Difference or Gini index of adoption rates across groups (e.g., age_group or group_id).

metrics.name: policy_effect_size
metrics.description: Change in adoption trend pre- vs post-mandate or campaign (e.g., difference-in-differences).

metrics.name: convergence_time
metrics.description: Number of steps until adoption rate change stays below a small threshold for a set lookback window.

metrics.name: peak_adoption_rate
metrics.description: Maximum observed adoption rate over the simulation period.

key_patterns.name: Heterogeneous risk-driven adoption
key_patterns.description: Agents with higher risk_perception are more likely to wear masks initially and adopt sooner post-exposure.
key_patterns.relevance: Set individual susceptibility and initial adoption probabilities; stratify calibration by risk_perception quantiles.

key_patterns.name: Layered diffusion with strong family influence
key_patterns.description: Family ties are few but strong; work/school are moderate; community is broad but weaker per tie.
key_patterns.relevance: Weight influence by layer; prioritize family transmissions for early cascades.

key_patterns.name: Complex contagion behavior
key_patterns.description: Adoption probability rises nonlinearly with the fraction/number of adopting neighbors; multiple exposures often precede adoption.
key_patterns.relevance: Use threshold or logistic-with-saturation functions rather than simple independent transmission.

key_patterns.name: Information precedes adoption
key_patterns.description: received_info typically becomes true before wearing_mask; adoption hazard is higher after info arrival.
key_patterns.relevance: Model a two-stage process (info diffusion → behavior adoption) with distinct parameters.

key_patterns.name: Churn and partial reversions
key_patterns.description: Some agents drop mask-wearing after adopting; churn is lower when neighbor adoption remains high.
key_patterns.relevance: Include retention dynamics modulated by local social norms.

key_patterns.name: Homophily and clustering by age_group/occupation
key_patterns.description: Ties concentrate within the same age_group and occupation, especially in work/school and family layers.
key_patterns.relevance: Expect cluster-level cascades and unequal adoption across groups; calibrate group-specific parameters.

key_patterns.name: Early influencer concentration
key_patterns.description: Early adopters often have higher degree or overlap ties across multiple layers with the same alters.
key_patterns.relevance: When seeding or estimating Rb, account for degree and multiplex overlap.

key_distributions.name: Degree distribution per layer
key_distributions.description: family: low-degree, narrow; work_school: medium, possibly right-skewed; community: right-skewed/heavy-tailed.
key_distributions.parameters: For each layer L: mean_degree_L, variance_degree_L, tail index (if heavy-tailed).

key_distributions.name: Risk perception
key_distributions.description: Continuous 0–1; typically modeled well by a Beta distribution.
key_distributions.parameters: Fit Beta(α, β) to risk_perception; also compute quantiles (Q20, Q50, Q80).

key_distributions.name: Adoption latency
key_distributions.description: Time from first information exposure (or first neighbor adoption exposure) to adoption; right-skewed.
key_distributions.parameters: Lognormal or geometric: lognormal(μ, σ) in steps; or geometric(p_adopt_per_step).

key_distributions.name: Exposures-to-adoption
key_distributions.description: Number of adopting-neighbor exposure events before first adoption.
key_distributions.parameters: Negative binomial NB(r, p) or geometric with mean_exposures_before_adoption.

key_distributions.name: Churn (time-to-drop)
key_distributions.description: Duration from adoption to first drop; decreases with higher neighbor adoption.
key_distributions.parameters: Exponential/geometric baseline with rate λ_drop; modulated by local adoption.

key_distributions.name: Assortativity by adoption
key_distributions.description: Positive assortativity expected due to homophily and local norm reinforcement.
key_distributions.parameters: Newman assortativity coefficient r_adopt in [-1, 1] over the multiplex or per layer.

key_relationships.relationship: Positive association; higher risk_perception increases initial adoption probability.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate via logistic regression; expect moderate-to-strong (OR > 1.5 per +0.25 risk).

key_relationships.relationship: Receipt of information increases next-step adoption hazard.
key_relationships.strength: Quantify as hazard ratio; expect HR > 2 controlling for social exposure.

key_relationships.relationship: Nonlinear increasing function with threshold-like effects; concave after saturation.
key_relationships.strength: Fit spline or logistic with quadratic term; strong local effect within family layer.

key_relationships.relationship: Group differences in adoption trajectories (e.g., students vs white collar).
key_relationships.strength: Test via interaction terms; expected medium differences; use for inequality_of_adoption.

key_relationships.relationship: Higher degree correlates with earlier adoption and higher influence count.
key_relationships.strength: Partial correlation controlling for risk_perception; expected moderate.

variables: multiplex overlap (same pair in multiple layers)
key_relationships.relationship: Overlapped ties increase influence per dyad.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate as per-dyad multiplier > 1.2 relative to single-layer ties.

initial_adoption_rate.notes: Compute p0 = sum_1{wearing_mask_day0}/N. Use exact seeds from day 0 when possible.

initial_informed_rate.notes: Initialize information state; if missing day 0, use earliest observed day.

seed_selection_method.value: Use observed day-0 mask wearers as seeds; if synthetic run, sample seeds proportional to degree*risk_perception
seed_selection_method.notes: Preserves empirically plausible early influencer profile.

layer_influence_weights.notes: Relative weights per contact; calibrate by matching early Rb and adoption latency.

layer_contact_probabilities_per_step.notes: Probability of interacting with each neighbor per step; tune with exposure counts vs observed adoption timing.

edge_directionality.notes: Symmetrize edges and deduplicate per layer.

homophily_by_group.notes: Quantify as ratio of within-group edges to random-mixing expectation; used if generating or rewiring networks.

adoption_hazard_model.value: logit(p_adopt_it) = α + β1*frac_neighbors_adopt_it-1 + β2*(frac_neighbors_adopt_it-1)^2 + β3*received_info_it-1 + β4*risk_perception_i + β5*(risk_perception_i * frac_neighbors_adopt_it-1) + Σ_L γ_L*frac_neighbors_adopt_in_layer_L_it-1
adoption_hazard_model.notes: Fit via discrete-time hazard regression; include agent random effects if sufficient data.

complex_contagion_threshold.source: exposures-before-adoption derived from time series and network
complex_contagion_threshold.notes: Alternative to logistic: agent adopts when cumulative weighted exposures exceed K_i ~ Poisson(λ). Calibrate λ to match mean_exposures_before_adoption.

info_diffusion.notes: Two channels: social (neighbors) and exogenous. Fit via hazard model on received_info.

adoption_delay_distribution.source: time difference between info/exposure and adoption
adoption_delay_distribution.notes: Represents cognitive/behavioral delay after threshold is met.

drop_hazard.value: logit(p_drop_it) = δ0 + δ1*(1 - frac_neighbors_adopt_it-1) + δ2*(1 - risk_perception_i)
drop_hazard.notes: Expect δ1 > 0; calibrate to match adoption_churn_rate and persistence curves.

multiplex_overlap_multiplier.source: dyads connected in multiple layers vs single layer influence
multiplex_overlap_multiplier.notes: Multiply exposure weight if the same dyad exists in ≥2 layers.

exposure_window.source: fit to maximize predictive power of lagged neighbor adoption for current adoption
exposure_window.notes: Number of past steps to aggregate exposures for adoption/churn decisions.

mandate_effect.source: if known mandate dates; otherwise scenario parameter
mandate_effect.notes: Apply from policy start day; estimate by difference-in-differences if event exists in data.

targeting_rules.value: If campaign: prioritize low-risk_perception and low-adoption groups (age_group/occupation) with highest betweenness centrality
targeting_rules.notes: Optimizes cascade size subject to budget.

Rb_window.notes: Compute behavior reproduction number over first 3 steps after adoption events.

convergence_threshold.notes: Convergence when |adoption_rate_t - adoption_rate_t-1| < threshold for 5 consecutive steps.

calibration_strategy.calibration_approach: Use a two-stage estimation plus simulation-based refinement. Stage 1: Fit discrete-time hazard models. (A) received_info_t ~ lagged neighbor info/adoption and exogenous trend. (B) wearing_mask_t ~ lagged neighbor adoption (overall and per layer), received_info, risk_perception, and interactions; include random effects if data permits. Estimate parameters (α, β, γ, δ) and derive implied thresholds and delays. Stage 2: Initialize simulation with observed day-0 states and run forward using estimated parameters. Perform multi-objective optimization (e.g., Bayesian optimization or CMA-ES/ABC) to minimize distance between simulated and observed metrics: adoption_rate_over_time, mean_exposures_before_adoption, adoption_churn_rate, behavior_reproduction_number_Rb (early window), and assortativity_by_adoption trajectory. Use priors from Stage 1 and penalize deviation from fitted coefficients to avoid overfitting.
calibration_strategy.validation_strategy: Temporal cross-validation: fit on first 60–70% of days, validate on the remainder. Posterior predictive checks for all evaluation metrics. Hold out subgroups (e.g., one occupation) or ego-nets to test generalization. Compare observed vs simulated: (1) adoption_rate_over_time (RMSE), (2) time_to_50_percent_adoption, (3) Rb during early growth (t=1..Rb_window), (4) churn curves (survival of adoption), (5) mean_exposures_before_adoption distribution (KS statistic), (6) assortativity_by_adoption trend, and (7) inequality_of_adoption across age_group/occupation. Perform sensitivity analysis on layer_influence_weights and exposure_window; report parameter elasticities.
key_variables_to_calibrate: adoption_hazard_model coefficients (α, β1, β2, β3, β4, β5, γ_L)

file_summaries:
Semantic metadata summary for agent_attributes.csv

- Data structure and type
  - CSV; flat, rectangular table.
  - One row per agent; no nesting. Suitable for direct load into a DataFrame or dict of agents.

- Columns and meanings
  - agent_id (int): Unique agent identifier; primary key for joins (e.g., to network edges).
  - age_group (categorical): Demographic cohort (e.g., Youth, Young Adult, Middle Age); can proxy for norms, susceptibility, and contact patterns.
  - occupation (categorical): Role/environment (e.g., Student, Blue Collar, White Collar); informs daily context and network layer (school, workplace, community).
  - risk_perception (float 0–1): Agent-specific perceived risk level; higher values indicate greater concern/aversion to infection.

- Relationships or nested elements
  - None within the file; each row is independent.
  - Intended external relationships: agent_id links to social network edges or location schedules; age_group/occupation define subgroup memberships and homophily.

- How this data informs the simulation
  - Agent initialization
    - Create agents keyed by agent_id; attach age_group, occupation, risk_perception traits.
    - Optionally derive initial mask_wearing state with P(mask_0) = f(risk_perception, age_group, occupation).
  - Decision dynamics
    - risk_perception modulates adoption threshold/sensitivity to social influence and public signals.
    - age_group and occupation can set baseline compliance, influence weights, and responsiveness heterogeneity.
  - Network/interaction structure
    - occupation maps agents to interaction layers (school vs workplace) and degree distributions.
    - age_group and occupation drive homophily for tie formation and layer-specific contact rates.
  - Policy/experiment hooks
    - Targeted interventions by subgroup (e.g., students) or by risk_perception quantiles.
    - Shock updates to risk_perception from information campaigns; track behavior diffusion conditioned on these attributes.

Semantic metadata summary for social_network.json

- Overall structure and type:
  - JSON object representing a multiplex (multi-layer) social network.
  - Top-level is a dictionary keyed by agent IDs (as strings), each mapping to an object with three adjacency lists.

- Meaning of keys/columns:
  - Top-level keys (e.g., "0", "1", "2"): unique agent identifiers (convertible to integers).
  - Nested keys:
    - family: list of agent IDs connected via household/familial ties.
    - work_school: list of agent IDs connected via workplace/school ties.
    - community: list of agent IDs connected via broader community ties (neighbors, friends, social groups).

- Relationships and nested elements:
  - Each agent has up to three lists of neighbors, one per layer. Lists are unweighted and imply presence of a tie in that context.
  - The network is layer-specific; the same pair may or may not appear in multiple layers.
  - Directionality is not explicit; treat edges as undirected if reciprocity is enforced in the full file, otherwise as directed or symmetrize during preprocessing.
  - IDs in lists reference other agents in the same global index space.

- How this informs simulation entities/interactions:
  - Agents: instantiate one agent per top-level key with state variables (e.g., mask_wearing: bool/probability; susceptibility to influence; layer-specific conformity).
  - Layers/contexts: model three interaction contexts with different contact frequencies and influence strengths (e.g., family > work_school > community for tie strength).
  - Interaction scheduling: at each time step, sample contacts from each layer per agent using layer-specific rates; propagate mask-wearing via social influence along listed ties.
  - Influence mechanics: assign layer weights or transmission probabilities per layer; optionally different thresholds or reinforcement if multiple layers connect the same pair.
  - Preprocessing notes: convert keys to ints; ensure neighbor IDs exist; deduplicate per list; decide on undirected vs directed handling; allow agents with empty lists in some layers.

- Data structure and type: Flat CSV time series. Each row is a snapshot of an individual agent’s state on a specific day. Composite key (day, agent_id). Boolean-like fields use true/false strings.
- Columns and meanings:
  - day (int): Discrete simulation time step.
  - agent_id (int): Unique identifier for an agent; stable across days.
  - wearing_mask (bool): Agent’s behavioral state (mask adoption) on that day.
  - received_info (bool): Whether the agent has received mask-related information by that day.
- Relationships/nesting: No nested elements; relationships are temporal per agent across days. Events are state transitions:
  - Information acquisition: received_info changes false→true (and possibly back if non-monotonic).
  - Behavior adoption: wearing_mask changes false→true (and possibly back).
  - The earliest true per agent marks first adoption/info times.
- Implications for the simulation:
  - Initialize agents at day 0 using the first-day rows (seed mask wearers and informed agents).
  - Use longitudinal transitions to estimate/calidate mechanisms:
    - Info diffusion rate (hazard of received_info becoming true).
    - Adoption conditional on info and/or social influence (P[w_t+1 | received_info, peers]).
    - Persistence/decay if reversions exist.
  - Lacks explicit network topology; supply or infer a network separately (e.g., synthetic graph) and calibrate parameters so simulated time series match observed transitions.
  - Treat (day, agent_id) as unique; ensure booleans parsed correctly; detect and timestamp transitions for learning and validation.

model_plan.description: Agent-based, multiplex network diffusion model of mask-wearing adoption with two-stage dynamics (information reception then behavior), complex contagion, policy and media effects, churn, and dynamic homophily-driven rewiring. Trained on days 0–29 and used to predict days 30–39.

parameters.seed_selection: Use observed wearing_mask at earliest day as adopters; observed received_info as informed

behaviors.name: observe_neighbors
behaviors.description: Compute weighted neighbor adoption exposure per layer and overall (with overlap boost), possibly aggregated over a window.
behaviors.algorithm: For each person i: for each layer L, compute frac_L = weighted fraction adopting among neighbors encountered (Bernoulli contact per neighbor with prob p_L). Combine layers: frac_all = sum_L (w_L * frac_L) / sum_L (w_L). Apply overlap multiplier to dyads appearing in multiple layers when sampling exposures. Optionally average frac_all over past W days.

behaviors.name: update_belief
behaviors.description: Update informed state based on base hazard, neighbor influences, exogenous media, and policy messaging.
behaviors.algorithm: For non-informed i: compute p_info = 1 - (1 - info_hazard_base) * (1 - info_external_rate * media_reach * messaging_intensity * message_credibility) * product over adopting neighbors encountered of (1 - info_peer_effect). Draw Bernoulli(p_info) to set informed=true.

behaviors.name: decide_adopt
behaviors.description: Adoption decision using logistic hazard with complex contagion (quadratic term), info term, risk term, layer-specific effects, policy odds multiplier, and optional delay.
behaviors.algorithm: If already adopting => skip. If i is in stubborn subset => adoption only via mandate odds multiplier; otherwise: compute features: x = frac_all, x2 = x^2, info = 1 if informed, risk = risk_perception, layer terms (frac per layer). logit = alpha + b1*x + b2*x2 + gI*info + gR*risk + gXR*risk*x + gF*frac_family + gW*frac_work + gC*frac_comm. If mandate active, add log(policy_odds_multiplier) to logit. Adjust for utility difference: U = benefit_perceived - compliance_cost; add U to logit. p = sigmoid(logit). If adoption_function == 'threshold': maintain cumulative weighted exposures E_i; adopt when E_i >= K_i ~ Poisson(lambda). If logistic: draw Bernoulli(p) to create a pending adoption with delay d ~ LogNormal(mu_log, sigma_log); activate after d days if not dropped before.

behaviors.name: drop_mask
behaviors.description: Churn hazard increases when local adoption is low, with fatigue and risk moderation; minimum duration enforcement.
behaviors.algorithm: For adopters with time_since_adoption >= min_duration: compute n = frac_all; logit_drop = intercept + bN*(1 - n) + bR*(1 - risk) + f*(fatigue_rate * time_since_adoption). p_drop = min(cap, sigmoid(logit_drop) + dropout_base_rate). Draw Bernoulli(p_drop) to drop.

behaviors.name: rewire_social_ties
behaviors.description: Dynamic homophily-driven rewiring favoring same adoption status and same group ties.
behaviors.algorithm: With prob dynamic_rewire_prob per ego: pick a random edge (i,j). If adoption status differs and homophily_strength > 0, consider rewiring: sample k not connected to i with probability proportional to homophily (same adoption, same age_group/occupation) and swap edge (i,j)->(i,k) preserving degree.

modules.name: SocialNetworkEngine
modules.description: Maintains multiplex network, computes contact events and exposures, and performs homophily-based rewiring.

update_rule.pseudocode:
for each agent i:
  sample contacts per layer L by Bernoulli(p_contact_L) over i's neighbors in L
  compute frac_L(i) = (#contacts adopting in L) / (max(1, #contacts in L))
  if dyad (i,j) exists in multiple layers, multiply contribution by multiplex_overlap_multiplier
  frac_overall(i) = sum_L layer_weight_L * frac_L(i) / sum_L layer_weight_L
with probability dynamic_rewire_prob per ego i:
  select random neighbor j; if adoption_state[i] != adoption_state[j]:
    propose k not in neighbors(i) with probability proportional to homophily(adoption, age_group, occupation)
    rewire (i,j)->(i,k) if proposal accepted
emit signal.frac_neighbors_by_layer, signal.frac_neighbors_overall and exposures_by_layer
notes: Symmetrize edges once at init; maintain layer-specific adjacency.

modules.calibration_notes: Tune layer weights, contact probs, and overlap multiplier to match early Rb and exposure-to-adoption statistics.

modules.name: PolicyAndMessaging
modules.description: Activates mandates and broadcasts public health messages via media channels.

update_rule.pseudocode:
policy_active = (current_day >= mandate_start_day)
policy_odds_multiplier = policy_active ? policy_odds_multiplier : 1.0
messaging_intensity_effective = messaging_intensity * media_reach * message_credibility * (1 + 0.1*message_bias)
emit signals
notes: Penalty and enforcement are implicitly captured in policy_odds_multiplier and also reduce drop hazard.
campaign_start_day aligns messaging onset with mandate by default.

modules.calibration_notes: policy_odds_multiplier and messaging_intensity constrained by pre/post trends around day 10 (DiD).

modules.name: InfoDiffusion
modules.description: Updates each agent's informed state based on base hazard, peer adoption, and messaging signals.

update_rule.pseudocode:
for each non-informed agent i:
  peer_term = 1 - (1 - info_peer_effect_per_adopting_neighbor)^(expected_contacts_adopting)
  msg_term = info_external_rate * messaging_intensity_effective
  p_info = 1 - (1 - info_hazard_base) * (1 - peer_term) * (1 - msg_term)
  if rand() < p_info: informed[i] = True
emit signal.informed_flags
notes: expected_contacts_adopting approximated from frac_overall and degree/contact rates.
Observation noise can flip informed with low probability if needed.

modules.calibration_notes: Fit hazards on received_info transitions; constrain by observed info before adoption.

modules.name: SocialInfluenceAdoption
modules.description: Computes adoption hazards and executes adoption with optional delay, incorporating info, peers, risk, layers, and policy.

notes: Stubborn agents can still adopt under strong mandate via odds multiplier acting on utility; to model hard stubbornness, skip adoption unless policy_active is true.
Initial adopters fixed from day 0 data.

modules.calibration_notes: Calibrate logistic coefficients via discrete-time hazard fit; refine with simulation-based objective including churn and Rb.

modules.name: DropoutAndFatigue
modules.description: Models churn among adopters driven by low local adoption, low risk, and fatigue; enforces a minimum duration.

update_rule.pseudocode:
for each adopting agent i with time_since_adoption >= dropout_min_duration_days:
  n = frac_overall[i]
  logit_drop = drop_logit_intercept + drop_beta_one_minus_neighbor_frac*(1 - n) + drop_beta_one_minus_risk*(1 - risk_perception[i]) + fatigue_rate * time_since_adoption
  if policy_active: logit_drop -= log(1 + mandate_enforcement_strength)
  p_drop = min(dropout_probability_cap, sigmoid(logit_drop) + dropout_base_rate)
  drop_now = (rand() < p_drop)
  if drop_now: set adoption_state=false; reset time_since_adoption
emit signal.dropout_flags
notes: Policy reduces drop hazard to capture enforcement and norm effects.
Churn is attenuated by high neighbor adoption via (1 - n) term.

modules.calibration_notes: Fit to observed reversions and survival of adoption durations.

modules.name: AdoptionAggregator
modules.description: Aggregates daily observables and computes evaluation metrics inputs.

update_rule.pseudocode:
adoption_rate_daily[t] = mean_i(adoption_state[i])
by_group = groupby(age_group).mean(adoption_state)
final_adoption_rate = adoption_rate_daily[last]
time_to_50 = first t with adoption_rate_daily[t] >= 0.5
Rb_series[t] = (new_adopters_in_window[t]) / (active_adopters[t-1]) over window Rb_window
churn_rate_daily[t] = (#drops at t) / (#adopters at t-1)
mean_exposures_before_adoption = average exposures counted for adopting agents
assortativity_by_adoption = Newman assortativity over current adoption states
inequality_of_adoption = difference or Gini across groups specified by inequality_group_field
policy_effect_size = slope_post - slope_pre around mandate_start_day
info_rate_daily[t] = mean_i(informed[i])
peak_adoption_rate = max_t adoption_rate_daily[t]
emit all observables
notes: Rb computed over a sliding window (default 3 days) for early-phase comparability.
Inequality_by_adoption uses age_group by default; configurable.

modules.calibration_notes: Not calibrated; used as target signals for other modules.

            num_agents = len(self.agents)
            avg_degree = int(max(2, int(self.config.get("avg_degree", 8))))
            k = max(2, avg_degree - (avg_degree % 2))
            p_rewire = float(self.config.get("small_world_rewiring_prob", 0.1))
            G = nx.watts_strogatz_graph(n=num_agents, k=k, p=p_rewire, seed=self.config.get("rng_seed", 42))
            adjacency_all = {i: set() for i in self.agents.keys()}
            for u, v in G.edges():
                adjacency_all[u].add(v)
                adjacency_all[v].add(u)

            # Randomly assign each undirected edge to one or more layers with probabilities approximating weights
            fam, wor, com = {i: set() for i in self.agents}, {i: set() for i in self.agents}, {i: set() for i in self.agents}
            for u, vs in adjacency_all.items():
                for v in vs:
                    if v < u:
                        continue
                    r = self.rng.random()
                    if r < 0.33:
                        fam[u].add(v); fam[v].add(u)
                    elif r < 0.66:
                        wor[u].add(v); wor[v].add(u)
                    else:
                        com[u].add(v); com[v].add(u)
                    # Some overlap chance
                    if self.rng.random() < 0.1:
                        extra = rs_choice(["family", "work_school", "community"], self.rng)
                        if extra == "family":
                            fam[u].add(v); fam[v].add(u)
                        elif extra == "work_school":
                            wor[u].add(v); wor[v].add(u)
                        else:
                            com[u].add(v); com[v].add(u)

            self.network = SocialNetwork(
                topology_type="small_world",
                adjacency_family=fam,
                adjacency_work_school=wor,
                adjacency_community=com,
                adjacency_all=adjacency_all,
                homophily_strength=self.homophily_strength
            )

        # Compute overlap counts
        self.overlap_counts.clear()
        for i, agent in self.agents.items():
            nf = self.network.adjacency_family.get(i, set())
            nw = self.network.adjacency_work_school.get(i, set())
            nc = self.network.adjacency_community.get(i, set())
            all_union = set().union(nf, nw, nc)
            for j in all_union:
                layers = int((j in nf)) + int((j in nw)) + int((j in nc))
                self.overlap_counts[tuple(sorted((i, j)))] = layers
        # Degree
        self.degrees = {i: len(self.network.adjacency_all.get(i, set())) for i in self.agents}
        for i, deg in self.degrees.items():
            self.agents[i].degree = deg

    def compute_daily_exposures(self) -> Tuple[Dict[int, float], Dict[int, Dict[str, float]], Dict[int, float]]:
        """
        Compute per-agent overall neighbor adoption fractions and per-layer fractions based on sampled contacts.

        Returns:
        - frac_overall: dict agent_id -> overall weighted adoption fraction among contacted neighbors.
        - frac_by_layer: dict agent_id -> dict layer_name -> layer-specific adoption fraction among contacts.
        - exposures_weighted_adopting: dict agent_id -> total weighted adopting contacts for exposure accounting.
        """
        pass
        frac_overall: Dict[int, float] = {}
        frac_by_layer: Dict[int, Dict[str, float]] = {}
        exposures_weighted_adopting: Dict[int, float] = {}

        # Precompute adopter states for speed
        adopter_state = {i: int(agent.adoption_state) for i, agent in self.agents.items()}

        for i, agent in self.agents.items():
            contacted_layers: Dict[str, set] = {
                "family": set(),
                "work_school": set(),
                "community": set(),
            }
            # Sample contacts per layer
            for layer, adj in [
                ("family", self.network.adjacency_family),
                ("work_school", self.network.adjacency_work_school),
                ("community", self.network.adjacency_community),
            ]:
                neighs = adj.get(i, set())
                p_contact = self.layer_contact_probs.get(layer, 0.0)
                for j in neighs:
                    if self.rng.random() < p_contact:
                        contacted_layers[layer].add(j)

            # Compute per-layer fractions
            by_layer = {}
            total_weighted = 0.0
            total_weighted_adopt = 0.0

            # For exposures counting unique neighbors across layers with overlap multiplier
            contacted_all_unique = set().union(*contacted_layers.values())
            weighted_adopting_contacts = 0.0

            # Compute per-layer fractions naive
            for layer_name in ["family", "work_school", "community"]:
                contacts = list(contacted_layers[layer_name])
                if contacts:
                    adopters = sum(adopter_state.get(j, 0) for j in contacts)
                    by_layer[layer_name] = adopters / float(len(contacts))
                else:
                    by_layer[layer_name] = 0.0

            # Combine layers with weights and overlap multiplier applied at the individual neighbor level
            for j in contacted_all_unique:
                layers_present = [L for L in ["family", "work_school", "community"] if j in contacted_layers[L]]
                if not layers_present:
                    continue
                weight_sum = sum(self.layer_weights[L] for L in layers_present)
                # Apply overlap multiplier if multi-layer contact today
                if len(layers_present) >= 2:
                    weight_sum *= self.overlap_multiplier
                total_weighted += weight_sum
                total_weighted_adopt += weight_sum * adopter_state.get(j, 0)
                weighted_adopting_contacts += weight_sum * adopter_state.get(j, 0)

            overall = (total_weighted_adopt / total_weighted) if total_weighted > 0 else 0.0
            frac_overall[i] = overall
            frac_by_layer[i] = by_layer
            exposures_weighted_adopting[i] = weighted_adopting_contacts

        # Maintain rolling window if needed (not explicitly used but kept for extensibility)
        self.buffer_frac_overall.append(frac_overall.copy())
        if len(self.buffer_frac_overall) > self.exposure_window:
            self.buffer_frac_overall.pop(0)

        return frac_overall, frac_by_layer, exposures_weighted_adopting

    def rewire_step(self):
        """
        Perform dynamic homophily-driven rewiring with probability per ego (dynamic_rewire_prob).
        Prefers replacement ties that match adoption state and group attributes (age_group/occupation).
        """
        pass
        if self.dynamic_rewire_prob <= 0.0:
            return

        for i, agent in self.agents.items():
            if self.rng.random() >= self.dynamic_rewire_prob:
                continue
            # Pick a random neighbor j from combined adjacency
            neighbors = list(self.network.adjacency_all.get(i, set()))
            if not neighbors:
                continue
            j = rs_choice(neighbors, self.rng)
            # If adoption status same, skip rewiring
            if self.agents.get(j) and (self.agents[j].adoption_state == agent.adoption_state):
                continue

            # Candidate pool: nodes not connected to i and not i
            all_nodes = list(self.agents.keys())
            neighbors_set = self.network.adjacency_all.get(i, set())
            candidate_k = [k for k in all_nodes if k != i and k not in neighbors_set]
            if not candidate_k:
                continue

            # Homophily score: 1 + strength * (1{same adoption} + 0.5*1{same group attributes})
            scores = []
            for k in candidate_k:
                a_same = int(self.agents[k].adoption_state == agent.adoption_state)
                g_same = 0
                g_same += int(self.agents[k].age_group == agent.age_group)
                g_same += int(self.agents[k].occupation == agent.occupation)
                g_same = 1 if g_same > 0 else 0
                score = 1.0 + self.homophily_strength * (a_same + 0.5 * g_same)
                scores.append(score)
            # Normalize
            total = sum(scores) if scores else 1.0
            probs = [s / total for s in scores]
            # Sample k proportional to scores
            r = self.rng.random()
            cum = 0.0
            k_selected = candidate_k[-1]
            for idx, p in enumerate(probs):
                cum += p
                if r <= cum:
                    k_selected = candidate_k[idx]
                    break

            # Rewire edge (i, j) -> (i, k_selected) across all layers where (i,j) exists
            for layer_name, adj in [
                ("family", self.network.adjacency_family),
                ("work_school", self.network.adjacency_work_school),
                ("community", self.network.adjacency_community)
            ]:
                if j in adj.get(i, set()):
                    # Remove old
                    adj[i].discard(j)
                    adj[j].discard(i)
                    # Add new
                    adj.setdefault(i, set()).add(k_selected)
                    adj.setdefault(k_selected, set()).add(i)
            # Update combined adjacency
            # Rebuild i's combined neighbors
            all_i = set().union(
                self.network.adjacency_family.get(i, set()),
                self.network.adjacency_work_school.get(i, set()),
                self.network.adjacency_community.get(i, set()),
            )
            self.network.adjacency_all[i] = all_i
            # Rebuild for old j and new k
            all_j = set().union(
                self.network.adjacency_family.get(j, set()),
                self.network.adjacency_work_school.get(j, set()),
                self.network.adjacency_community.get(j, set()),
            )
            self.network.adjacency_all[j] = all_j
            all_k = set().union(
                self.network.adjacency_family.get(k_selected, set()),
                self.network.adjacency_work_school.get(k_selected, set()),
                self.network.adjacency_community.get(k_selected, set()),
            )
            self.network.adjacency_all[k_selected] = all_k

        # Recompute overlap counts after rewiring
        self.overlap_counts.clear()
        for i, agent in self.agents.items():
            nf = self.network.adjacency_family.get(i, set())
            nw = self.network.adjacency_work_school.get(i, set())
            nc = self.network.adjacency_community.get(i, set())
            all_union = set().union(nf, nw, nc)
            for j in all_union:
                layers = int((j in nf)) + int((j in nw)) + int((j in nc))
                self.overlap_counts[tuple(sorted((i, j)))] = layers

    def assortativity_by_adoption(self) -> float:
        """
        Compute assortativity coefficient of the combined network with respect to adoption_state attribute.

        Returns:
        - Newman assortativity coefficient r in [-1, 1].
        """
        pass
        try:
            G = nx.Graph()
            for i in self.agents.keys():
                G.add_node(i, adoption=int(self.agents[i].adoption_state))
            for i, neighs in self.network.adjacency_all.items():
                for j in neighs:
                    if j > i:
                        G.add_edge(i, j)
            if G.number_of_edges() == 0:
                return 0.0
            r = nx.attribute_assortativity_coefficient(G, "adoption")
            if math.isnan(r):
                return 0.0
            return float(r)
        except Exception:
            return 0.0


class PolicyAndMessaging:
    """
    PolicyAndMessaging module that activates mandates and computes effective messaging intensity signals.

    Exposed signals:
    - policy_active: bool
    - policy_odds_multiplier: float
    - messaging_intensity_effective: float
    """
    def __init__(self, pha: PublicHealthAuthority, media: MediaChannel, config: Dict[str, Any]):
        """
        Initialize with public health authority, media, and configuration.
        """
        pass
        self.pha = pha
        self.media = media
        self.config = config
        # Read parameters
        self.policy_odds_multiplier_cfg = float(config.get("policy_odds_multiplier", 1.0))

    def step(self, current_day: int) -> Tuple[bool, float, float]:
        """
        Update policy and messaging signals for the current day.

        Returns:
        - policy_active
        - policy_odds_multiplier
        - messaging_intensity_effective
        """
        pass
        self.pha.issue_mandate(current_day)
        self.pha.adjust_policy(current_day)
        policy_active = bool(self.pha.mandate_active)
        policy_odds_mult = self.policy_odds_multiplier_cfg if policy_active else 1.0

        return policy_active, policy_odds_mult, messaging_intensity_effective


class InfoDiffusion:
    """
    InfoDiffusion module updates the 'informed' flag for each agent based on hazards:
    - base hazard
    - peer effect from adopting neighbors (approximate via overall neighbor adoption fraction)
    - external messaging effect (from PolicyAndMessaging signals)
    """
    def __init__(self, agents: Dict[int, Person], config: Dict[str, Any], rng: random.Random):
        """
        Initialize InfoDiffusion with agents, configuration, and RNG.
        """
        pass
        self.agents = agents
        self.config = config
        self.rng = rng

    def step(self, frac_overall: Dict[int, float], messaging_intensity_effective: float,
             mean_contact_prob: float) -> Dict[int, bool]:
        """
        Perform a single-day update of informed states.

        Args:
        - frac_overall: dict agent_id -> overall adoption fraction among neighbors from SocialNetworkEngine.
        - messaging_intensity_effective: effective intensity of external messaging.
        - mean_contact_prob: approximate mean contact probability used to scale peer exposures.

        Returns:
        - informed_flags: dict agent_id -> bool indicating informed status at end of step.
        """
        pass
        base = float(self.config.get("info_hazard_base", 0.05))
        peer_eff = float(self.config.get("info_peer_effect_per_adopting_neighbor", 0.02))
        external_rate = float(self.config.get("info_external_rate", 0.01))

        # Compute degree-based expected adopting contacts approximation
        informed_flags: Dict[int, bool] = {}
        for i, agent in self.agents.items():
            if agent.informed:
                informed_flags[i] = True
                continue
            frac = float(frac_overall.get(i, 0.0))
            degree = max(0, agent.degree)
            expected_contacts_adopting = frac * degree * mean_contact_prob
            # Peer term using per-contact hazard approximation: 1 - (1 - peer_eff)^k
            peer_term = 1.0 - ((1.0 - peer_eff) ** max(0.0, expected_contacts_adopting))
            msg_term = external_rate * max(0.0, messaging_intensity_effective)
            p_info = 1.0 - (1.0 - base) * (1.0 - peer_term) * (1.0 - msg_term)
            if self.rng.random() < p_info:
                informed_flags[i] = True
            else:
                informed_flags[i] = False

        # Update agents
        for i, flag in informed_flags.items():
            if flag:
                self.agents[i].informed = True

        return informed_flags


class SocialInfluenceAdoption:
    """
    SocialInfluenceAdoption module decides on adoption for non-adopting agents, using logistic or threshold models.
    """
    def __init__(self, agents: Dict[int, Person], config: Dict[str, Any], rng: random.Random):
        """
        Initialize with agents, configuration, and RNG. Pre-select stubborn agents.
        """
        pass
        self.agents = agents
        self.config = config
        self.rng = rng

        # Adoption model coefficients
        self.alpha = float(config.get("adoption_logit_alpha", -2.0))
        self.b1 = float(config.get("adoption_beta_neighbors", 3.0))
        self.b2 = float(config.get("adoption_beta_neighbors_sq", 1.5))
        self.gI = float(config.get("adoption_gamma_info", 1.2))
        self.gR = float(config.get("adoption_gamma_risk", 0.8))
        self.gXR = float(config.get("adoption_gamma_risk_x_neighbors", 0.5))
        self.gF = float(config.get("adoption_gamma_layer_family", 0.5))
        self.gW = float(config.get("adoption_gamma_layer_work", 0.3))
        self.gC = float(config.get("adoption_gamma_layer_community", 0.1))

        self.compliance_cost = float(config.get("compliance_cost", 0.2))
        self.benefit_perceived = float(config.get("benefit_perceived", 0.3))

        self.adoption_function = str(config.get("adoption_function", "logistic"))
        self.delay_mu = float(config.get("adoption_delay_mu_log", 0.0))
        self.delay_sigma = float(config.get("adoption_delay_sigma_log", 0.75))
        self.threshold_lambda = float(config.get("adoption_threshold_lambda", 2.0))

        # Build stubborn set
        stubborn_fraction = float(config.get("stubborn_fraction", 0.1))
        ids = list(self.agents.keys())
        n_stubborn = int(round(stubborn_fraction * len(ids)))
        # Sample inversely proportional to risk_perception
        weights = []
        for i in ids:
            w = max(1e-6, 1.0 - float(self.agents[i].risk_perception))
            weights.append(w)
        total = sum(weights) if weights else 1.0
        probs = [w / total for w in weights]
        chosen = set()
        # Weighted sampling without replacement
        while len(chosen) < n_stubborn and ids:
            r = self.rng.random()
            cum = 0.0
            sel_idx = len(ids) - 1
            for idx, p in enumerate(probs):
                cum += p
                if r <= cum:
                    sel_idx = idx
                    break
            chosen.add(ids[sel_idx])
            # Remove and renormalize
            ids.pop(sel_idx)
            probs.pop(sel_idx)
            if probs:
                s = sum(probs)
                probs = [p / s for p in probs]
        for i in chosen:
            self.agents[i].stubborn = True

        # Track scheduled adoptions: agent_id -> days_remaining
        self.scheduled: Dict[int, int] = {}

    def step(self, frac_overall: Dict[int, float], frac_by_layer: Dict[int, Dict[str, float]],
             policy_active: bool, policy_odds_multiplier: float,
             exposures_weighted_adopting: Dict[int, float], current_day: int) -> Dict[int, bool]:
        """
        Execute adoption decisions for the day, including scheduled activations.

        Args:
        - frac_overall: dict agent_id -> overall fraction adopting among neighbors.
        - frac_by_layer: dict agent_id -> dict layer_name -> fraction adopting among contacts in that layer.
        - policy_active: whether a mandate is active.
        - policy_odds_multiplier: odds multiplier applied when policy is active.
        - exposures_weighted_adopting: dict agent_id -> weighted adopting contacts for exposure accounting.
        - current_day: current simulation day.

        Returns:
        - adoption_flags: dict agent_id -> bool indicating if agent is adopting at end of step.
        """
        pass
        adoption_flags: Dict[int, bool] = {}

        # Decrease scheduled delays and activate adoptions
        to_activate = []
        for aid, days_rem in list(self.scheduled.items()):
            days_rem -= 1
            self.scheduled[aid] = days_rem
            if days_rem <= 0:
                to_activate.append(aid)
        for aid in to_activate:
            agent = self.agents.get(aid)
            if agent and not agent.adoption_state:
                agent.wear_mask()
                agent.first_adoption_day = current_day
            self.scheduled.pop(aid, None)

        for i, agent in self.agents.items():
            if agent.adoption_state:
                adoption_flags[i] = True
                continue

            x = float(frac_overall.get(i, 0.0))
            x2 = x * x
            info = 1.0 if agent.informed else 0.0
            risk = float(agent.risk_perception)
            layer_terms = 0.0
            layers = frac_by_layer.get(i, {})
            layer_terms += self.gF * float(layers.get("family", 0.0))
            layer_terms += self.gW * float(layers.get("work_school", 0.0))
            layer_terms += self.gC * float(layers.get("community", 0.0))
            logit = self.alpha + self.b1 * x + self.b2 * x2 + self.gI * info + self.gR * risk + self.gXR * risk * x + layer_terms
            # Policy odds multiplier
            if policy_active:
                logit += math.log(max(1.0, float(policy_odds_multiplier)))
            # Utility difference
            U = float(self.benefit_perceived) - float(self.compliance_cost)
            logit += U

            # Stubbornness: can still adopt if policy strongly increases odds; here we allow but reduce probability if no policy
            if agent.stubborn and not policy_active:
                # Reduce logit substantially for stubborn absent policy
                logit -= 2.0

            if self.adoption_function == "logistic":
                p_adopt = sigmoid(logit)
                if self.rng.random() < p_adopt:
                    # Schedule with delay
                    delay = lognormal_delay(self.delay_mu, self.delay_sigma, self.rng)
                    if delay <= 0:
                        agent.wear_mask()
                        agent.first_adoption_day = current_day
                    else:
                        self.scheduled[i] = delay
            else:
                # Threshold model
                agent.cumulative_exposures += float(exposures_weighted_adopting.get(i, 0.0))
                K = max(0.5, float(self.threshold_lambda))
                if agent.cumulative_exposures >= K:
                    delay = lognormal_delay(self.delay_mu, self.delay_sigma, self.rng)
                    if delay <= 0:
                        agent.wear_mask()
                        agent.first_adoption_day = current_day
                    else:
                        self.scheduled[i] = delay

            adoption_flags[i] = bool(agent.adoption_state)

            # Track exposures before adoption for metrics
            if not agent.adoption_state:
                agent.exposures_before_adoption += float(exposures_weighted_adopting.get(i, 0.0))

        return adoption_flags


class DropoutAndFatigue:
    """
    DropoutAndFatigue module computes daily dropout decisions among adopters based on:
    - baseline dropout
    - local neighbor adoption fraction (1 - n)
    - low risk (1 - risk_perception)
    - fatigue accumulation
    - policy reduces dropout hazard via enforcement
    """
    def __init__(self, agents: Dict[int, Person], config: Dict[str, Any], rng: random.Random):
        """
        Initialize with agents, configuration, and RNG.
        """
        pass
        self.agents = agents
        self.config = config
        self.rng = rng
        self.base = float(config.get("dropout_base_rate", 0.01))
        self.fatigue_rate = float(config.get("fatigue_rate", 0.005))
        self.intercept = float(config.get("drop_logit_intercept", -4.0))
        self.bN = float(config.get("drop_beta_one_minus_neighbor_frac", 2.0))
        self.bR = float(config.get("drop_beta_one_minus_risk", 1.5))
        self.min_duration = int(config.get("dropout_min_duration_days", 2))
        self.cap = float(config.get("dropout_probability_cap", 0.5))

    def step(self, frac_overall: Dict[int, float], policy_active: bool, enforcement_strength: float) -> Dict[int, bool]:
        """
        Execute dropout decisions for adopters with sufficient duration.

        Args:
        - frac_overall: dict agent_id -> overall neighbor adoption fraction.
        - policy_active: bool; whether mandate active reduces dropout odds.
        - enforcement_strength: float scaling of dropout reduction when policy is active.

        Returns:
        - dropout_flags: dict agent_id -> bool indicating whether the agent has dropped at this step.
        """
        pass
        dropout_flags: Dict[int, bool] = {}
        for i, agent in self.agents.items():
            if not agent.adoption_state:
                dropout_flags[i] = False
                continue
            agent.time_since_adoption += 1
            # Fatigue accumulation
            agent.fatigue += self.fatigue_rate
            if agent.time_since_adoption < self.min_duration:
                dropout_flags[i] = False
                continue

            n = float(frac_overall.get(i, 0.0))
            logit_drop = self.intercept + self.bN * (1.0 - n) + self.bR * (1.0 - float(agent.risk_perception)) + (agent.fatigue)
            if policy_active:
                logit_drop -= math.log(1.0 + max(0.0, enforcement_strength))
            p_drop = min(self.cap, sigmoid(logit_drop) + self.base)
            agent.dropout_probability = p_drop
            if self.rng.random() < p_drop:
                agent.drop_mask()
                dropout_flags[i] = True
            else:
                dropout_flags[i] = False
        return dropout_flags


class AdoptionAggregator:
    """
    AdoptionAggregator module computes daily observables and helper metrics for evaluation:

def sigmoid(x: float) -> float:
    """
    Compute the sigmoid function.
    Returns a value between 0 and 1.

    This helper function is used for logistic hazard computations across adoption and dropout processes.
    """
    pass
    try:
        if x < -700:
            return 0.0
        return 1.0 / (1.0 + math.exp(-x))
    except Exception:
        return 0.5


def gini_coefficient(values: List[float]) -> float:
    """
    Compute the Gini coefficient for a list of non-negative values.
    Returns a float in [0, 1]. If values sum to zero, returns 0.

    Notes:
    - This is used to compute inequality_of_adoption across groups.
    """
    pass
    if not values:
        return 0.0
    arr = np.array(values, dtype=float)
    if np.all(arr == 0):
        return 0.0
    arr = np.sort(arr)
    n = arr.shape[0]
    cum = np.cumsum(arr)
    gini = (n + 1 - 2 * np.sum(cum) / cum[-1]) / n
    return float(gini)

def lognormal_delay(mu_log: float, sigma_log: float, rng: random.Random) -> int:
    """
    Sample a discrete delay from a lognormal distribution with parameters on log scale.
    Returns a non-negative integer number of days.
    """
    pass
    # Use scipy.stats.lognorm to obtain RV; shape = sigma, scale = exp(mu)
    try:
        shape = max(1e-6, float(sigma_log))
        scale = float(math.exp(mu_log))
        rv = lognorm(s=shape, scale=scale)
        delay = rv.rvs(random_state=rng)  # uses numpy random if seedless; but we pass python rng, so approximate with uniform draw
        # To use rng consistently, sample U and inverse CDF
        u = rng.random()
        delay = rv.ppf(u)
        return max(0, int(round(delay)))
    except Exception:
        # Fallback to simple geometric-like integer with mean ~exp(mu)
        m = max(0.0, math.exp(mu_log))
        return max(0, int(round(m)))

def rmse(y_true: List[float], y_pred: List[float]) -> float:
    """
    Compute Root Mean Square Error between two sequences. Returns NaN if lengths mismatch or zero length.
    """
    pass
    if not y_true or not y_pred or len(y_true) != len(y_pred):
        return float("nan")
    arr_true = np.array(y_true, dtype=float)
    arr_pred = np.array(y_pred, dtype=float)
    return float(np.sqrt(np.mean((arr_true - arr_pred) ** 2)))


def mae(y_true: List[float], y_pred: List[float]) -> float:

    arr_true = np.array(y_true, dtype=float)
    arr_pred = np.array(y_pred, dtype=float)
    return float(np.mean(np.abs(arr_true - arr_pred)))

class SocialNetworkEngine:
    """
    SocialNetworkEngine maintains multiplex adjacency, computes daily exposures and layer-specific neighbor adoption fractions,
    and performs homophily-based rewiring.

    Key parameters are taken from the configuration dictionary, including:
    - layer weights and contact probabilities
    - dynamic rewiring probability
    - homophily strength
    - multiplex overlap multiplier
    - exposure window for rolling aggregation

    Methods:
    - build_or_load_network: Load from JSON if available, else generate synthetic network.
    - compute_daily_exposures: For each agent, sample layer contacts and compute weighted neighbor adoption fractions.
    - rewire_step: With a probability per ego, rewire one tie towards homophily.
    - assortativity_by_adoption: Compute assortativity coefficient for the combined graph based on adoption state.
    """
    def __init__(self, agents: Dict[int, Person], config: Dict[str, Any], rng: random.Random):
        """
        Initialize the SocialNetworkEngine with agents and configuration.

        Args:
        - agents: Dictionary mapping agent ids to Person objects.
        - config: Configuration parameters including network and layer properties.
        - rng: Random number generator for reproducible stochastic operations.
        """
        pass
        self.agents = agents
        self.config = config
        self.rng = rng
        self.layer_weights = {
            "family": float(config.get("layer_weight_family", 0.6)),
            "work_school": float(config.get("layer_weight_work", 0.3)),
            "community": float(config.get("layer_weight_community", 0.1)),
        }
        self.layer_contact_probs = {
            "family": float(config.get("layer_contact_prob_family", 0.9)),
            "work_school": float(config.get("layer_contact_prob_work", 0.6)),
            "community": float(config.get("layer_contact_prob_community", 0.25)),
        }
        self.dynamic_rewire_prob = float(config.get("dynamic_rewire_prob", 0.02))
        self.homophily_strength = float(config.get("homophily_strength", 0.2))
        self.overlap_multiplier = float(config.get("multiplex_overlap_multiplier", 1.3))
        self.exposure_window = int(config.get("exposure_window", 3))
        self.multi_layer_network = bool(config.get("multi_layer_network", True))

        # Internal state
        self.network = SocialNetwork()
        self.overlap_counts: Dict[Tuple[int, int], int] = {}
        self.degrees: Dict[int, int] = {}

        # Rolling memory for exposures
        self.buffer_frac_overall: List[Dict[int, float]] = []

    def _symmetrize(self, adj: Dict[int, set]) -> Dict[int, set]:
        """
        Symmetrize a given adjacency dictionary to ensure undirected edges.

        Returns a new adjacency dictionary with mutual links.
        """
        pass
        out = {i: set(neigh) for i, neigh in adj.items()}
        for i, neigh in adj.items():
            for j in neigh:
                out.setdefault(j, set()).add(i)
                out.setdefault(i, set()).add(j)
        return out

    def build_or_load_network(self, data_files: Dict[str, str]):
        """
        Load observed multiplex network from JSON if available; otherwise, generate a small-world inspired synthetic network
        and randomly assign edges to layers.

        The resulting adjacency is stored in self.network, and overlap counts are precomputed.
        """
        pass
        json_path = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, data_files.get("social_network.json", "social_network.json"))
        loaded = False
        if os.path.exists(json_path):
            try:
                with open(json_path, "r") as f:
                    data = json.load(f)
                # Convert keys to ints and lists to sets while deduplicating
                fam, wor, com, all_adj = {}, {}, {}, {}
                for k_str, v in data.items():
                    i = try_int(k_str)
                    if i is None:
                        continue
                    fam[i] = set(try_int(x) for x in v.get("family", []) if try_int(x) is not None)
                    wor[i] = set(try_int(x) for x in v.get("work_school", []) if try_int(x) is not None)
                    com[i] = set(try_int(x) for x in v.get("community", []) if try_int(x) is not None)
                    all_set = set()
                    all_set.update(fam[i] if i in fam else set())
                    all_set.update(wor[i] if i in wor else set())
                    all_set.update(com[i] if i in com else set())
                    all_adj[i] = all_set
                fam = self._symmetrize(fam)
                wor = self._symmetrize(wor)
                com = self._symmetrize(com)
                all_adj = self._symmetrize(all_adj)

                self.network = SocialNetwork(
                    topology_type="observed_multiplex",
                    adjacency_family=fam,
                    adjacency_work_school=wor,
                    adjacency_community=com,
                    adjacency_all=all_adj,
                    homophily_strength=self.homophily_strength
                )
                loaded = True
            except Exception as e:
                print("Error loading social network JSON; falling back to synthetic generation:", e)

        if not loaded:
            # Synthetic generation: small-world on all agents; assign edges to layers randomly based on Dirichlet-proportions approximating layer weights
            num_agents = len(self.agents)
            avg_degree = int(max(2, int(self.config.get("avg_degree", 8))))
            k = max(2, avg_degree - (avg_degree % 2))
            p_rewire = float(self.config.get("small_world_rewiring_prob", 0.1))
            G = nx.watts_strogatz_graph(n=num_agents, k=k, p=p_rewire, seed=self.config.get("rng_seed", 42))
            adjacency_all = {i: set() for i in self.agents.keys()}
            for u, v in G.edges():
                adjacency_all[u].add(v)
                adjacency_all[v].add(u)

            # Randomly assign each undirected edge to one or more layers with probabilities approximating weights
            fam, wor, com = {i: set() for i in self.agents}, {i: set() for i in self.agents}, {i: set() for i in self.agents}
            for u, vs in adjacency_all.items():
                for v in vs:
                    if v < u:
                        continue
                    r = self.rng.random()
                    if r < 0.33:
                        fam[u].add(v); fam[v].add(u)
                    elif r < 0.66:
                        wor[u].add(v); wor[v].add(u)
                    else:
                        com[u].add(v); com[v].add(u)
                    # Some overlap chance
                    if self.rng.random() < 0.1:
                        extra = rs_choice(["family", "work_school", "community"], self.rng)
                        if extra == "family":
                            fam[u].add(v); fam[v].add(u)
                        elif extra == "work_school":
                            wor[u].add(v); wor[v].add(u)
                        else:
                            com[u].add(v); com[v].add(u)

            self.network = SocialNetwork(
                topology_type="small_world",
                adjacency_family=fam,
                adjacency_work_school=wor,
                adjacency_community=com,
                adjacency_all=adjacency_all,
                homophily_strength=self.homophily_strength
            )

        # Compute overlap counts
        self.overlap_counts.clear()
        for i, agent in self.agents.items():
            nf = self.network.adjacency_family.get(i, set())
            nw = self.network.adjacency_work_school.get(i, set())
            nc = self.network.adjacency_community.get(i, set())
            all_union = set().union(nf, nw, nc)
            for j in all_union:
                layers = int((j in nf)) + int((j in nw)) + int((j in nc))
                self.overlap_counts[tuple(sorted((i, j)))] = layers
        # Degree
        self.degrees = {i: len(self.network.adjacency_all.get(i, set())) for i in self.agents}
        for i, deg in self.degrees.items():
            self.agents[i].degree = deg

    def compute_daily_exposures(self) -> Tuple[Dict[int, float], Dict[int, Dict[str, float]], Dict[int, float]]:
        """
        Compute per-agent overall neighbor adoption fractions and per-layer fractions based on sampled contacts.

        Returns:
        - frac_overall: dict agent_id -> overall weighted adoption fraction among contacted neighbors.
        - frac_by_layer: dict agent_id -> dict layer_name -> layer-specific adoption fraction among contacts.
        - exposures_weighted_adopting: dict agent_id -> total weighted adopting contacts for exposure accounting.
        """
        pass
        frac_overall: Dict[int, float] = {}
        frac_by_layer: Dict[int, Dict[str, float]] = {}
        exposures_weighted_adopting: Dict[int, float] = {}

        # Precompute adopter states for speed
        adopter_state = {i: int(agent.adoption_state) for i, agent in self.agents.items()}

        for i, agent in self.agents.items():
            contacted_layers: Dict[str, set] = {
                "family": set(),
                "work_school": set(),
                "community": set(),
            }
            # Sample contacts per layer
            for layer, adj in [
                ("family", self.network.adjacency_family),
                ("work_school", self.network.adjacency_work_school),
                ("community", self.network.adjacency_community),
            ]:
                neighs = adj.get(i, set())
                p_contact = self.layer_contact_probs.get(layer, 0.0)
                for j in neighs:
                    if self.rng.random() < p_contact:
                        contacted_layers[layer].add(j)

            # Compute per-layer fractions
            by_layer = {}
            total_weighted = 0.0
            total_weighted_adopt = 0.0

            # For exposures counting unique neighbors across layers with overlap multiplier
            contacted_all_unique = set().union(*contacted_layers.values())
            weighted_adopting_contacts = 0.0

            # Compute per-layer fractions naive
            for layer_name in ["family", "work_school", "community"]:
                contacts = list(contacted_layers[layer_name])
                if contacts:
                    adopters = sum(adopter_state.get(j, 0) for j in contacts)
                    by_layer[layer_name] = adopters / float(len(contacts))
                else:
                    by_layer[layer_name] = 0.0

            # Combine layers with weights and overlap multiplier applied at the individual neighbor level
            for j in contacted_all_unique:
                layers_present = [L for L in ["family", "work_school", "community"] if j in contacted_layers[L]]
                if not layers_present:
                    continue
                weight_sum = sum(self.layer_weights[L] for L in layers_present)
                # Apply overlap multiplier if multi-layer contact today
                if len(layers_present) >= 2:
                    weight_sum *= self.overlap_multiplier
                total_weighted += weight_sum
                total_weighted_adopt += weight_sum * adopter_state.get(j, 0)
                weighted_adopting_contacts += weight_sum * adopter_state.get(j, 0)

            overall = (total_weighted_adopt / total_weighted) if total_weighted > 0 else 0.0
            frac_overall[i] = overall
            frac_by_layer[i] = by_layer
            exposures_weighted_adopting[i] = weighted_adopting_contacts

        # Maintain rolling window if needed (not explicitly used but kept for extensibility)
        self.buffer_frac_overall.append(frac_overall.copy())
        if len(self.buffer_frac_overall) > self.exposure_window:
            self.buffer_frac_overall.pop(0)

        return frac_overall, frac_by_layer, exposures_weighted_adopting

    def rewire_step(self):
        """
        Perform dynamic homophily-driven rewiring with probability per ego (dynamic_rewire_prob).
        Prefers replacement ties that match adoption state and group attributes (age_group/occupation).
        """
        pass
        if self.dynamic_rewire_prob <= 0.0:
            return

        for i, agent in self.agents.items():
            if self.rng.random() >= self.dynamic_rewire_prob:
                continue
            # Pick a random neighbor j from combined adjacency
            neighbors = list(self.network.adjacency_all.get(i, set()))
            if not neighbors:
                continue
            j = rs_choice(neighbors, self.rng)
            # If adoption status same, skip rewiring
            if self.agents.get(j) and (self.agents[j].adoption_state == agent.adoption_state):
                continue

            # Candidate pool: nodes not connected to i and not i
            all_nodes = list(self.agents.keys())
            neighbors_set = self.network.adjacency_all.get(i, set())
            candidate_k = [k for k in all_nodes if k != i and k not in neighbors_set]
            if not candidate_k:
                continue

            # Homophily score: 1 + strength * (1{same adoption} + 0.5*1{same group attributes})
            scores = []
            for k in candidate_k:
                a_same = int(self.agents[k].adoption_state == agent.adoption_state)
                g_same = 0
                g_same += int(self.agents[k].age_group == agent.age_group)
                g_same += int(self.agents[k].occupation == agent.occupation)
                g_same = 1 if g_same > 0 else 0
                score = 1.0 + self.homophily_strength * (a_same + 0.5 * g_same)
                scores.append(score)
            # Normalize
            total = sum(scores) if scores else 1.0
            probs = [s / total for s in scores]
            # Sample k proportional to scores
            r = self.rng.random()
            cum = 0.0
            k_selected = candidate_k[-1]
            for idx, p in enumerate(probs):
                cum += p
                if r <= cum:
                    k_selected = candidate_k[idx]
                    break

            # Rewire edge (i, j) -> (i, k_selected) across all layers where (i,j) exists
            for layer_name, adj in [
                ("family", self.network.adjacency_family),
                ("work_school", self.network.adjacency_work_school),
                ("community", self.network.adjacency_community)
            ]:
                if j in adj.get(i, set()):
                    # Remove old
                    adj[i].discard(j)
                    adj[j].discard(i)
                    # Add new
                    adj.setdefault(i, set()).add(k_selected)
                    adj.setdefault(k_selected, set()).add(i)
            # Update combined adjacency
            # Rebuild i's combined neighbors
            all_i = set().union(
                self.network.adjacency_family.get(i, set()),
                self.network.adjacency_work_school.get(i, set()),
                self.network.adjacency_community.get(i, set()),
            )
            self.network.adjacency_all[i] = all_i
            # Rebuild for old j and new k
            all_j = set().union(
                self.network.adjacency_family.get(j, set()),
                self.network.adjacency_work_school.get(j, set()),
                self.network.adjacency_community.get(j, set()),
            )
            self.network.adjacency_all[j] = all_j
            all_k = set().union(
                self.network.adjacency_family.get(k_selected, set()),
                self.network.adjacency_work_school.get(k_selected, set()),
                self.network.adjacency_community.get(k_selected, set()),
            )
            self.network.adjacency_all[k_selected] = all_k

        # Recompute overlap counts after rewiring
        self.overlap_counts.clear()
        for i, agent in self.agents.items():
            nf = self.network.adjacency_family.get(i, set())
            nw = self.network.adjacency_work_school.get(i, set())
            nc = self.network.adjacency_community.get(i, set())
            all_union = set().union(nf, nw, nc)
            for j in all_union:
                layers = int((j in nf)) + int((j in nw)) + int((j in nc))
                self.overlap_counts[tuple(sorted((i, j)))] = layers

    def assortativity_by_adoption(self) -> float:
        """
        Compute assortativity coefficient of the combined network with respect to adoption_state attribute.

        Returns:
        - Newman assortativity coefficient r in [-1, 1].
        """
        pass
        try:
            G = nx.Graph()
            for i in self.agents.keys():
                G.add_node(i, adoption=int(self.agents[i].adoption_state))
            for i, neighs in self.network.adjacency_all.items():
                for j in neighs:
                    if j > i:
                        G.add_edge(i, j)
            if G.number_of_edges() == 0:
                return 0.0
            r = nx.attribute_assortativity_coefficient(G, "adoption")
            if math.isnan(r):
                return 0.0
            return float(r)
        except Exception:
            return 0.0
